answer: Each identity locks collateral in a bonded escrow, so splitting stake among aliases does not erase liability: when k coordinated identities equivocate, pairwise evidence triggers a slash proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²). The protocol’s asymmetric depreciation compounds the loss across implicated bonds, giving a jade-and-opal sybil swarm an exponential capital-loss multiplier upon detection—not the fable of costless identities.
